sections.heading: Beyond decir
sections.body:
Good reported speech uses precise verbs. They fall into two groups by the mood that follows:

- **Reporting information → indicative**: *afirmar* (to state), *asegurar* (to assure), *explicar*, *contar*, *comentar*, *mencionar*, *confesar* (to confess), *admitir / reconocer* (to admit), *prometer* (to promise — often + conditional: *Prometió que llegaría a tiempo*), *anunciar*, *advertir* (to warn — informational: *Advirtió que habría retrasos*).
- **Influencing / requesting → subjunctive**: *pedir, rogar* (to beg), *exigir* (to demand), *sugerir, recomendar, aconsejar, ordenar, insistir en, advertir* (warning someone to do something: *Nos advirtió que no saliéramos*).

sections.heading: Negated reporting verbs
sections.body: When the speaker denies the statement, the subjunctive appears: *Negó que lo supiera.* (He denied knowing it.) *No dijo que fuera culpa suya.* (He didn't say it was his fault.) Compare *No dijo que era culpa suya* — also used, when the speaker treats it as a fact he merely didn't mention.

sections.heading: Summarising rather than quoting
sections.body: Often you report the act rather than the words: *Me felicitó por el ascenso.* (He congratulated me on the promotion.) *Se quejó del servicio.* (She complained about the service.) *Me agradeció la ayuda.* (He thanked me for the help.) *Se disculpó por llegar tarde.* (She apologised for being late.) *Me invitó a cenar.*

examples: He stated that he knew nothing.
She confessed that she had lied.
He admitted he had made a mistake.
She promised she'd arrive on time.
They announced there would be delays.
He warned us not to go out.
Me rogó que no se lo dijera a nadie.
She begged me not to tell anyone.
El cliente exigió que le devolvieran el dinero.
No dijo que fuera culpa suya.
He didn't say it was his fault.
He congratulated me on the promotion.
He thanked me for the help.
